newsitem.title: USA: Clinton extends American, pilots labor talks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton extends American, pilots labor talks.

text.p: President Clinton has given a labour mediator two additional days to try to reach a labour settlement between American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp., and its pilots, spokesman Mike McCurry said on Monday.

He said Clinton acted in response to a letter from presidential emergency board Chairman Robert Harris that said the two sides were in "intensive" mediation and the additional time would increase the chances of settlement.

Under the law, the mediator had until Monday to submit proposals to Clinton on how to settle the dispute over pay and whether APA pilots or other pilots would fly the new commuter jets American plans buy.

McCurry also said American and the Allied Pilots Association agreed there would be no work stoppage until April 28 at the earliest, well beyond the 60-day period during which there could be no strike or lockout under the federal law that governs airline labour relations.
Clinton created the board Feb. 15, ending a brief strike staged by the pilots after a week of intensive talks had failed to produce a new contract.
Under the law, the board had 30 days to recommend a new contract and the two sides 30 days more to consider it.
